Kathmandu, August 29

More than Rs 5 billion has been deposited into the Prime Minister’s Relief Fund for the rescue and relief of people affected by the devastating Bhotekoshi floods.

Prime Minister Balen Shah said Rs 5.04 billion has been deposited into accounts maintained at nine commercial banks.

According to Shah, an additional US$1.8 million has been deposited into accounts at Himalayan Bank and Laxmi Bank.

The funds have been collected to support rescue and relief efforts for people stranded and affected by the floods.

Shah urged individuals and organisations wishing to contribute to use only the government’s officially published QR code and bank accounts to ensure transparency and prevent possible financial fraud.

“In this difficult disaster situation, we request everyone to provide financial assistance only through the government’s officially published QR code and accounts under the names ‘Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund’ and ‘Prime Minister’s Relief Fund’ to ensure transparent use and proper management of assistance and to prevent possible financial fraud,” Shah said.

Kathmandu, August 29

The immediate risk of a lake burst from a water body formed after an ice-rock avalanche in Rasuwa has decreased, according to technical experts.

The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology said the possibility of the lake suddenly bursting has reduced after water began flowing out naturally. Experts have also warned that rumours of an imminent lake burst have affected ongoing search and rescue operations in downstream areas.

Binod Parajuli, chief of the Flood Forecasting Division at the department, said the risk of a sudden breach has declined as the newly formed lake has already started overflowing.

“Normally, unstable lakes burst soon after filling up. This lake has filled and started releasing water, and more than 24 hours have passed without a breach,” Parajuli said. “Once water begins flowing out, the possibility of the lake bursting decreases.”

Geologist Shri Kamal Dwivedi, who works at the Secretariat of the Water and Energy Commission, said the water body formed in a depression created after an ice-rock fall should not necessarily be considered a lake at risk of bursting.

“Water filling a depression and flowing out is different from a lake bursting,” Dwivedi said, adding that unnecessary rumours about a possible flood had affected rescue and search operations downstream.

After Wednesday’s devastating flood, a drone survey conducted by China in the northern region of Langtang Lirung identified two water bodies — one at around 4,000 metres above sea level and another in the upper section of Lhende Khola.

At the time, both water bodies were considered potentially risky as water levels were rising. However, recent images and data show that one outlet has opened and water is gradually draining, according to officials.

Experts estimate the two water bodies hold around 50,000 cubic metres of water. They said even in the worst-case scenario, a possible breach would not produce a flood as destructive as the one seen last Wednesday, when an estimated 20 million cubic metres of water and debris swept downstream.

Parajuli said the current concern is that fresh landslides could fall into the water bodies and trigger renewed flooding.

“The flood debris from Wednesday has already raised the riverbed. If another flood occurs, there could be risks along the riverbanks,” he said.

Experts said further monitoring of the water bodies, including their depth and volume, is ongoing through satellite images and drone data. While the immediate threat has decreased, authorities have advised continued vigilance.

Kathmandu, August 29

At least 898 people remain unaccounted for after devastating floods in the Bhotekoshi River swept through hydropower project areas in Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

According to data provided by the Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal (IPPAN), 11 hydropower projects in the two districts have been affected by the floods. Rescue teams have so far evacuated 361 people from the affected project sites.

A large number of those rescued were employees and workers at the 216 MW Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project. IPPAN said 254 people have been rescued from the project alone.

However, around 300 people are still believed to be trapped inside the project’s tunnel.

The Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation said a team of Chinese experts has also arrived in Nepal to assist in the rescue of those trapped inside the tunnel.

Similarly, 18 people have been rescued from the 20 MW Langtang Khola Hydropower Project and 91 from the 37 MW Upper Trishuli-3B Hydropower Project.

Seven hydropower projects affected in Rasuwa

According to IPPAN, seven hydropower projects in Rasuwa have been affected by the Bhotekoshi floods.

They are the 216 MW Upper Trishuli-1, 111 MW Rasuwa Gadhi, 120 MW Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi, 6.42 MW Upper Mailung-A, 20 MW Langtang Khola, 22 MW Chilime and 5 MW Mailung Khola hydropower projects.

The direct impact of the floods on these project sites has raised concerns about the safety of employees and workers.

With communication cut off with people at several project sites, search and rescue operations have been prioritised.

Six projects affected in Nuwakot

Six hydropower and energy projects in Nuwakot have also been affected.

The affected projects are the 24 MW Trishuli, 14.1 MW Devighat, 60 MW Upper Trishuli-3A, 37 MW Upper Trishuli-3B, 15.6 MW Middle Trishuli Ganga and 25 MW Nuwakot Solar Power Project.

Workers trapped inside tunnels pose major rescue challenge

Rescuing people trapped inside project structures, particularly tunnels, has emerged as the biggest challenge following the floods.

The estimated 300 people trapped inside the Upper Trishuli-1 tunnel highlight the complexity of the rescue operation. Additional technical expertise and specialised rescue teams are being mobilised to reach them.

The arrival of Chinese experts is expected to provide additional technical support for the tunnel rescue.

Search and rescue operations are continuing in the flood-affected areas, and further details on those still unaccounted for are expected as teams reach more project sites.

The latest figures indicate that while 361 people have been rescued, 898 remain unaccounted for.

The scale of the crisis shows that the Bhotekoshi floods have caused more than damage to hydropower infrastructure. They have created a major humanitarian emergency involving hundreds of workers and employees stationed at the affected projects.

The immediate priority remains establishing contact with those unaccounted for and rescuing them wherever possible.

As bodies swept away by Wednesday’s floods continue to be recovered across several districts, authorities are facing a new challenge: there is simply not enough space to store them. […]

The post Why is the govt temporarily burying unidentified bodies recovered from Rasuwa floods? appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.

]]>

Kathmandu, August 29

The devastating floods in Rasuwa’s Bhotekoshi River have killed more than 600 people, but most of the bodies recovered so far remain unidentified.

As bodies swept away by Wednesday’s floods continue to be recovered across several districts, authorities are facing a new challenge: there is simply not enough space to store them.

Some bodies have already begun decomposing in the heat, creating a growing risk of foul odour, infection and public-health problems. With morgues and available refrigerated storage unable to accommodate the large number of bodies, the government has decided to temporarily bury unidentified bodies until they can be identified and handed over to their families.

But why was burial chosen? How will the identities of the dead be preserved? And what happens if relatives come looking for a body later?

Here is what officials and forensic experts say.

Why are the bodies being buried?

The immediate reason is the lack of adequate facilities to store such a large number of bodies.

According to Nepal Police, bodies have so far been recovered in Rasuwa, Dhading, Gorkha, Nawalparasi East, Nuwakot, Chitwan, Tanahun and Nawalparasi West.

Chitwan has recorded the highest number, with 233 bodies recovered, followed by 158 in Nawalparasi East, 54 in Gorkha, 49 in Dhading, 47 in Nawalparasi West, 41 in Nuwakot, 31 in Tanahun and 13 in Rasuwa.

Relatives of many of the victims have also been unable to reach the recovery sites because roads have been destroyed or remain inaccessible.

The large number of bodies recovered at once has overwhelmed existing morgues and refrigerated storage facilities.

According to the Ministry of Health, government and private health institutions across Nepal have refrigerated capacity for around 600 bodies. However, much of that capacity cannot be used for the flood victims because the bodies have been recovered across geographically dispersed districts.

In Chitwan alone, health facilities have a combined capacity to store only around 50 bodies. Even that capacity has been strained, with some hospital freezers already occupied by unidentified bodies.

Authorities say there was not enough time or available infrastructure to immediately establish additional cold-storage facilities, temporary morgues or refrigerated containers.

As a result, temporary burial has been adopted as a last-resort preservation measure.

Police Inspector Anil Thapa says decomposition has already begun.

“The bodies have started decomposing. As decomposition progresses, the smell is spreading. We are burying them to prevent the risk of epidemics and infection,” Thapa said.

According to him, the smell has begun spreading up to 1.5 to two kilometres from some locations where bodies are being kept, affecting patients at nearby hospitals as well as local residents.

Why not simply keep the bodies in cold storage?

Refrigeration remains the preferred option when large numbers of bodies are recovered after a disaster.

International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) guidance recommends keeping bodies at around 2–4 degrees Celsius in refrigerated containers or other suitable cold-storage facilities wherever possible.

But when adequate refrigeration is unavailable, temporary burial in a safe location can be used to preserve the bodies until they can be identified and returned to their families.

Senior forensic expert Dr Gopal Chaudhary of Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital says temporary burial is not the same as a final funeral.

“Temporary burial means documenting all the details of the deceased, taking photographs and DNA samples, and burying the body underground in a safe place until relatives come forward,” he said.

The objective, therefore, is not to dispose of unidentified bodies but to preserve them in a way that allows identification and recovery later.

Why couldn’t additional morgues or refrigerated containers be set up?

The scale and geographical spread of the disaster have made the problem more complicated.

Bodies have been recovered from several districts stretching from Rasuwa towards Chitwan and Nawalparasi. No single hospital or institution has enough capacity to store all of them for an extended period.

Hospitals normally have morgues designed for routine requirements, not for hundreds of bodies arriving simultaneously following a major disaster.

At the same time, authorities have to carry out postmortems, document bodies, photograph identifying features and collect DNA samples.

In Chitwan, Bharatpur Hospital has formed seven forensic teams to carry out postmortems and collect DNA samples, with forensic specialists from hospitals including Bheri Hospital and Lumbini also providing assistance.

With existing storage facilities overwhelmed and additional refrigerated infrastructure not immediately available, officials opted for temporary burial.

How will the bodies be buried?

Authorities say the bodies will not be dumped together in an unidentified mass grave.

Each body will be individually documented and assigned a unique identification number before burial.

The documentation includes photographs of the face, tattoos, injuries, scars and other distinguishing physical features. Clothing and other belongings found with the body will also be recorded.

A legal document will be prepared for each body, while DNA samples will be collected and preserved.

More than 100 bodies had already undergone DNA profiling by Saturday afternoon and were being prepared for burial.

Bodies began being buried on Saturday afternoon in a forested area between Ramnagar and Devghat in Bharatpur Metropolitan City-1, according to the authorities.

The graves are being dug to a depth of around 1.5 metres while avoiding damage to the surrounding sal trees. A gap of around 40 centimetres will be maintained between individual bodies.

The body bags will carry identification numbers, and corresponding markers will be placed at the burial sites.

Authorities will also photograph and record the burial process and maintain GPS coordinates and mapping data showing the exact location of each body.

The burial area will subsequently be fenced off or otherwise secured.

What happens if a body is later identified?

Temporary burial does not close the possibility of identification or recovery.

If relatives later come forward, authorities can compare information provided by the family with the records, photographs and other evidence collected before burial.

DNA testing can then be used to confirm the identity.

If a match is established, the body can be exhumed and handed over to the family for funeral rites according to their religious and cultural practices.

Inspector Thapa said the burial system has been designed specifically to make such future recovery possible.

“If a DNA match is established in the future and the family wants to perform the final rites according to their religion and culture, the body can be exhumed and handed over to them,” he said.

Dr Chaudhary said the same procedure can be followed by comparing DNA from relatives with samples collected from the bodies.

What happens to body parts recovered separately?

The floods have severely damaged some bodies, and body parts have been recovered separately from different locations.

These will also be documented and preserved in the same manner as complete bodies.

DNA samples and identification numbers will be assigned so that individual remains can potentially be linked to a victim later.

Will the bodies decompose underground?

Yes. Burial does not stop decomposition.

However, forensic experts say decomposition can be slower underground than when a body is exposed in the open.

According to Dr Chaudhary, the rate of decomposition is comparatively slower underground, meaning a body may remain in a relatively better state for a period of time.

The purpose of burial is therefore not to prevent decomposition indefinitely. Rather, it is to slow the process, control the immediate public-health and environmental problems caused by exposed bodies, and preserve the possibility of identification and future exhumation.

Why is location and record-keeping so important?

The entire process is designed to ensure that authorities can locate an individual body even years after burial.

Each body will have a unique identification number. The same number will be recorded in official documents, on a marker associated with the burial site and in forensic records.

GPS coordinates, photographs and videos of the burial location will also be preserved.

A concrete marker indicating the identification number will be placed near each burial site so that the location of a particular body can be traced later.

Has Nepal used temporary burial before?

Yes. A similar system was used following the 2015 earthquake when unidentified bodies had to be managed after existing facilities were overwhelmed.

According to Dr Chaudhary, 32 bodies were temporarily buried on the premises of Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital following the earthquake.

Some foreign families came searching for their missing relatives years later. DNA testing helped identify two of the bodies, which were subsequently exhumed and handed over to their families.

Dr Chaudhary says around 30 bodies buried during the earthquake still remain on the teaching hospital premises.

How long must unidentified remains be preserved?

According to Dr Chaudhary, Nepal’s legal provisions require unidentified bodies and remains to be preserved for an extended period.

He says unidentified bodies and remaining bones or other remains are required to be preserved for up to 12 years.

“If relatives come looking for them within those 12 years, the remains must also be handed over,” he said.

After that period, legal provisions allow the person to be declared dead.

So, why bury the bodies now?

The decision is essentially the result of three immediate problems coming together: the unusually high number of bodies, insufficient refrigerated storage, and rapid decomposition caused by the heat.

Burial was not chosen as a substitute for identification or as a final disposal method. It was chosen because authorities needed a way to move the bodies away from overcrowded and unsuitable storage conditions while preserving every possible means of identifying them later.

Each body is therefore being documented, photographed, assigned a unique number, sampled for DNA and mapped before being buried.

For the families still searching for their missing loved ones, the crucial point is that burial does not mean the search for identity ends. The system is intended to ensure that a body can still be traced, identified and exhumed when a family comes forward.

Nepal News https://english.nepalnews.com Sat, 29 Aug 2026 17:35:14 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1 https://english.nepalnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/cropped-favicon-01-32x32.png Nepal News https://english.nepalnews.com 32 32 Unidentified bodies to be inhumed after keeping DNA safe https://english.nepalnews.com/s/nation/unidentified-bodies-to-be-inhumed-after-keeping-dna-safe/ EXAMPLE-PERSON-26 Sat, 29 Aug 2026 16:05:15 +0000 https://english.nepalnews.com/?p=239177 KATHMANDU: The management of dead bodies in unrecognizable condition has begun with the burial after keeping their DNA safe.

The dead bodies were retrieved from various places following the catastrophic flash flood that ripped through Rasuwa district on August 26.

The inhumation of the unidentified bodies is being carried out as per the ‘Directive on Management of Unidentified Bodies and Unattended Dead Bodies (first amendment), 2026’.

The government is forwarding the process to inter the corpses by keeping the DNA and other marks safe. Later, the inhumed bodies will however be exhumed and handed over to the concerned families for last rites with the DNA ‘matching’.

The Directive has a provision that if the heir of the deceased one is identified in the future, the interred body or organ should be exhumed and handed over to the family in a respectful manner.

Spokesperson at the Ministry of Home Affairs, Anand Kafle, made it clear that the ongoing efforts to management dead bodies were in line with the law.

He refuted the attempts made to create confusion among public on management of the corpses. “We have followed the Directive while managing the dead bodies. We have also completed scientific process. So, we request the public not to spread confusion on this issue.”

In this connection, a public health expert at the Epidemiology and Disease Control Division under the Department of Health Services, Dr Amrit Pokharel, said, “The risk of public health may increase once the dead bodies are left unattended for a long time. That’s why, underground management of the bodies is essential.”

Collecting DNA samples of the unidentified bodies and human organs and keeping them safe before inhumation is a scientific and responsible move, he reminded.

As the government protects the DNA samples of each corpse, the relatives of the deceased would be able to identify these later. Each body is given a separate and unique identification number.

Since the records such as the details of the body, identification number and DNA samples are kept safely, anyone claiming to be their relative can identify by undergoing scientific testing.

The Directive has finely mentioned the respectful handover of the deceased one to the respective family/heirs once they are identified in the future. The government follows the very Directive while managing the corpses, it is informed.

]]> How journalism became an addiction for a female Tharu crusader https://english.nepalnews.com/s/opinion/how-journalism-became-an-addiction-for-a-female-tharu-crusader/ EXAMPLE-PERSON-33 Sat, 29 Aug 2026 14:27:11 +0000 https://english.nepalnews.com/?p=239148 Most of the history of the community I represent remains unwritten. Even in this age of technology, many positive aspects of the Tharu community have not been documented.

The Tharu community has its own language, art, and culture. It has its own way of living life. However, finding these things when searching in books was difficult. Ever since I was in school, I felt that someone should write down and preserve the ancestral knowledge and skills possessed by our parents.

The access of people from the Tharu community to justice, education, and healthcare was weak. I personally suffered the pain of being looked down upon due to language alone. For these very reasons, journalism gradually became more than just a profession for me—it became like an addiction.

In this 2-decade-long journey, I earned praise from many. At the same time, I also faced threats on numerous occasions. I remember that during COVID-19, news stories I wrote prompted immediate positive decisions from the cabinet meeting of Sudurpashchim Province.

Whether it was the incident of Rajkumari Rana and Radha Chaudhary, who were beaten on allegations of witchcraft, or the incident of Maya BK, who was gang-raped and murdered, I feel that the news stories I wrote provided some assistance in the process of delivering justice to them. I can never forget the respect I received from those families.

Interviewing Bishna Chaudhary, ward member of Baguliya, Ghodaghodi Municipality-3, about how public representatives are utilizing technology

At a time when various rumors were spreading about the Tikapur incident, I believe the words I wrote helped dispel those misconceptions to some extent and aided in documenting the history of the Tharu community.

For me, the greatest attraction of journalism is having the opportunity to write not only on human rights issues concerning women, Indigenous nationalities, Tharus, Dalits, and marginalized communities, but also on matters linked to their indigenous skills, art, culture, and identity. However, the experiences while raising these issues are not easy. Around 2015, as voices for federalism grew louder, Tharu journalists reporting on the Tharuhat/Tharuwan movement had to take risks. That risk increased even further during the movement in the fiscal year 2015/16. The mistreatment I faced, not only from non-Tharu communities but also from the police administration, is something I cannot forget.

While writing about the history of political change brought about by the Tharuhat movement, I also had to endure criticism of Resham Chaudhary repeatedly. During the Gen Z protests, after I wrote a news story titled that party cadres themselves were involved in the vandalism at Sudurpashchim Province government offices, a situation arose where I had to leave home and live separately for one week. But I did not stop writing.

For me, those challenges became energy. The nib of my pen was never capped. Perhaps the joy found in writing is the true addiction of journalism. This very addiction makes one ready to take risks, in the hope that the words I have written will one day become pages of history.

From writing complaints to mainstream media

Once, I was a guerrilla warrior writing complaints in people’s courts during the People’s War. Today, transforming my writing, I am working in mainstream journalism. Back then as well, I tried to bring justice by writing complaints for helpless citizens who were subjected to injustice. Even now, I am striving to become a voice for the voiceless through journalism.

The year was 2005. After things did not go well at home, I left home in search of my future. That was an age just emerging from childhood. I could not find work anywhere. Ultimately, I became a full-time member of the then CPN (Maoist) and was given the responsibility of writing complaint applications for cases coming to the people’s court.

I wrote complaints for about six months. I covered my expenses with the small amount of money given by those who came to file complaints. I received Rs 5 per complaint. The memory of earning my livelihood from that money remains fresh even today.

Crossing by boat while heading to report from the flood-affected Bhajani Municipality

As my interest in writing grew, the party deployed me to the publicity department. In the fiscal year 2006/07, I started working as a hawker for the newspaper ‘Same Aawaj’, which was known as the mouthpiece of the Maoists.

At that time, I was completely ignorant about journalism. I wrote complaints for legal cases, but I had no knowledge of what news was or how to write it. Journalism was neither my subject of choice nor a desire. I entered this field solely to fulfill the responsibility assigned by the party.

My family never accepted my profession. However, I could not detach myself from it.

After joining the newspaper, I began receiving training from time to time on news writing and newspaper operations. Journalist Dipendra Rawal taught me the basics of news writing and reporting. Embracing those learnings, I tried to move forward.

In 2017, a news story was published under my byline for the first time in that newspaper. From that day on, my dedication to journalism grew even stronger.

However, journalism in Kailali was challenging at that time. Moreover, problems were even greater for female journalists. Even today, the number of female journalists in Kailali can be counted on one’s fingers. At that time, the situation was even harder. Only three to four women, including Logshari Kunwar and myself, were active in journalism.

Financial hardship was another major challenge.

I remember staying hungry for many days. Working as a volunteer, I had no money in my pocket. I could not even speak Nepali properly. To many, it seemed foolish for a woman from the Tharu community to leave her studies and family behind to seek a future in journalism.

Speaking with locals of Bhajani Municipality about the damage caused by the floods

I used to eat and stay at the office. One day, both rice and cooking gas ran out. Brother Dipendra had Rs 10 in his pocket. He gave me that money and sent me to buy jaggery. For two days, eating only that jaggery and drinking water, he and I worked on the newspaper.

My mentor in journalism, Rawal, is an injured veteran of the People’s War. Hit by shrapnel all over his body, he had joined the newspaper after returning from treatment at that time. Carrying shrapnel in his body to this day, he remains active in journalism.

In later days, journalism became the main path of my life. I have worked in more than half a dozen newspapers. However, because regional newspapers could not become financially viable, I had to work as a volunteer in many places.

Some of the newspapers I worked for have already shut down. JP Joshi, the editor of one newspaper where I worked, disappeared in the fiscal year 2008/09. After 55 days, his skeleton was found. That incident made me even more resilient.

Interacting with women who received employment under the Prime Minister Employment Program in Dhangadhi Sub-Metropolitan City-6

After that, I started working for a newspaper outside the party. The monthly salary was Rs 4,000, and even that arrived in installments. From that money, I had to arrange for food, clothing, and transportation all together.

Violence, attacks, and an unyielding pen

Around the fiscal year 2012/13, together with some journalist friends, we operated the newspaper ‘News Paschimeli’. I was its associate editor. From reporting to typesetting and marketing, I often had to handle the work myself. I would roam the market all day. In the evening, I would write news. At night, while setting the newspaper layout, it would become 12–1 AM.

One evening at around 8 PM, after finishing work, I left for my room. On the way, a man came from behind and grabbed my private parts. I screamed. He tried to assault me. My hand found a stone. Hitting him with that stone, I barely escaped.

After that, I filed complaints demanding action against the culprit at bodies including the Federation of Nepali Journalists (FNJ) Kailali Chapter and the District Police Office, Kailali. The administration could not arrest the attacker. However, following the voice I raised, a police post was established in that location. After that, I and other women and young girls walking on that road began to feel somewhat relieved and safer.

While practicing journalism, I have gathered many experiences where my writing made an immediate impact. I also remember incidents where news published under my byline was presented as documentary evidence in court, enabling victims to receive justice.

Social campaigning alongside journalism

Alongside journalism, I have been advocating and lobbying against injustice and oppression. I have even provided shelter to numerous women subjected to violence.

In incidents such as Rajkumari Rana, who was beaten under allegations of witchcraft in the fiscal year 2012/13, Radha Chaudhary, who was beaten by Bhole Baba on International Women’s Day, March 8, 2018, and Maya BK, who was gang-raped and murdered, many individuals, including myself, participated directly in campaigns to bring them justice.

I have particularly focused my writing on the rights and issues of Kamaiya (bonded laborers), Kamalhari (indentured female laborers), Dalits, women, Indigenous groups, and marginalized communities. I have also been actively advocating and lobbying on these issues.

Covering a street-corner assembly organized in Dhangadhi during the Tharuhat movement

Not only that, I have also been continuously raising my voice on issues linked to establishing the identity of the Tharu community and preserving cultures and traditions that are facing extinction. Some youth of the new generation who do not know me as a journalist recognize me as the “Sister who constructed the Gurhi statue.”

At a time when the Gurhi festival seemed to be on the verge of disappearing, starting from the fiscal year 2000/01, under my leadership, we began going to immerse Gurhi at present-day Gurhi Chowk (then Campus Chowk) in Dhangadhi. Initially, there were only two to four of us.

I had a single objective: to name that intersection Gurhi Chowk and to install a statue of Gurhi there.

Carrying that vision forward, the Sakhi Sanjal was formed in the fiscal year 2020/21 under the leadership of Indu Tharu. I became its vice president. I worked as the acting president for a long time and later assumed the responsibility of president.

At that time, campaigns even had to be run just to attend public events wearing traditional Tharu attire. There were many who felt embarrassed to wear Tharu clothing. I, however, stood proudly in Tharu attire, even if I was alone.

Over time, our group grew stronger. Along with naming the intersection, we also began lobbying the government for a local public holiday.

Ultimately, that location was established as Gurhi Chowk. A statue of Gurhi was erected at the intersection. The Sudurpashchim Province government even gazetted a local holiday in Kailali and Kanchanpur on the occasion of the Gurhi festival.

My journalism is inspired by events like these. Writing the unwritten stories of my community, speaking for those subjected to injustice, putting into words the culture and history fading into oblivion, and wishing that those words become proof of history one day, perhaps for this reason, journalism did not remain merely a profession for me, it became an addiction.

Addressing media representatives today, Foreign Minister Khanal addressed media reports circulating both nationally and internationally that suggested Nepal had declined external aid.

The Foreign Minister emphasized that reports alleging Nepal had rejected international assistance were entirely false. He clarified that given the immense scale of devastation, support and assistance remain vital for immediate rescue and relief efforts, and even more so for the upcoming phases of reconstruction and rehabilitation.

Highlighting that a detailed needs assessment is currently underway across affected critical infrastructure, road networks, and hydropower facilities, the Foreign Minister noted that specialized international assistance is already active on the ground. Specialized technical reconnaissance teams from India and China have been mobilized for complex operations, including tunnel rescues, while relief materials continue to arrive from international partners, including India, China, Japan, and Australia.

In addition to direct rehabilitation support, Foreign Minister Khanal emphasized that one of the most effective ways the international community can support Nepal’s recovery is through tourism and economic engagement.

He urged international travelers not to hesitate to visit, reassuring potential visitors that the country remains largely open for tourism. He pointed out that major destinations—including Pokhara, Lumbini, Chitwan, Janakpur, and most mountain regions—remain safe and accessible. He added that while the country is experiencing deep grief, its borders, supply chains, and general infrastructure continue to operate smoothly.

The government reiterated that foreign nationals and organizations wishing to assist can also contribute directly to the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund through secure online platforms as full-scale recovery efforts continue.

नवलपरासी। 

भाेटेकाेशी तथा त्रिशुलीकाे बाढीमा परि ज्यान गुमाएका मानिसहरूकाे नारायणी नदीबाट संकलित पहिचान नखुलेका शवहरूलाई सामुदायिक वनमा व्यवस्थापन गरिने भएकाे छ ।

विपद व्यवस्थापन तथा जिल्ला सुरक्षा समितिकाे निर्णय अनुसार पहिचान नखुलेका,शरीरका अङ्गहरू टुक्रिएकाे अवस्थामा फेला परेका शवहरूकाे डिएनए नमूना संकलन तथा पाेष्टमार्टम गरी कानुनी प्रकृया पूरा गरेर शवकाे व्यवस्थापन गर्न लागिएकाे जिल्ला प्रहरी प्रमुख युवराज खड्काले बताए ।

प्रउ खड्काका अनुसार जिल्लामा सुरक्षित र सुबिधा युक्त शवगृहकाे अभावमा भेटिएका शवहरू तराईको अत्यधिक गर्मीका कारण दिनदिनै गल्दै गई दुर्गन्धित पनि हुँदै गएकाेले जिल्लाका दुई सामुदायिक ज्याेतिकुञ र दिव्यपुरी वनमा पहिचानका लागि ट्यागहरू राखेर व्यवस्थापन गरिने भएकाे छ ।

नवलपरासी पूर्वकाे गैडनकाेट देखि त्रिवेणीसम्मकाे झण्डै १ सय किलोमिटर नारायणी नदीकाे तटीय क्षेत्रमा भाेटेकाेशी बाढी आएकाे भदौ १० गते साँझ देखिनै मानव शवहरू भेटिएका थिए ।

नदीमा भेटिएका शवहरूलाई प्रहरीले जिल्ला प्रशासन,सबै सुरक्षा अंङ्ग तथा स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधिहरूसंग समन्वय गरी जिल्लाका नगर अस्पताल,जिल्ला अस्पताल तथा हाेल्डिङसेन्टरमा सकेसम्म वातानुकुलित व्यवस्था गरी राखेकाे थियाे ।

संकलित शवकाे संख्यामा दिनहुँ बढाेत्तरी आएसंगै शव व्यवस्थापनका लागि स्थान अभाव हुँदै जाँदा विपद व्यवस्थापन समितिकै निर्णयमा वाह्य जिल्लासंग समन्वय गरी सुरक्षित व्यवस्थापन तथा पहिचानका लागि ४९ ओेटा शवलाई पाेखरा र पाल्पा पठाईएकाे प्रजिअ जगदिश्वर उपाध्यायले बताउनु भयाे ।

पहिचान नखुली रहेका शवहरूलाई व्यवारिसे शव व्यवस्थापन  निर्देशिका २०८३ अनुसार सकेसम्म पहिचानमा सहज रहने गरी सांकेतिक काेड सहितकाे नम्बर राखेर सुरक्षा घेरा वनाई अस्थायी संरक्षणका लागि शवकाे व्यवस्थापन गर्ने जिल्ला सुरक्षा समितिकाे तयारी रहेकाे बुझिएकाे छ ।

जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय नवलपरासी पूर्वका अनुसार बुधबार देखि शनिबार अवेर सम्म ४४ महिला ६३ पुरूष ११ बालक १२ बालिका र ५४ मानव शरीरका विभिन्न अंङ्ग गरी १ सय ८४ शव जिल्लाका विभिन्न प्रहरी युनिट अन्तर्गतका नारायणी नदी क्षेत्रमा भेटिएकाे छ ।

बाढीकाे उच्च बहाव र तिब्र गतिका कारण मानिसकाे हात, खुट्टा,टाउकाे, जाँघ, लगायत शरीरका अंङ्गहरू टुक्रिएकाे अवस्थामा अधिकाशं शवहरू भेटिएकाेले पहिचानमा समेत कठीनाई देखिएकाे हराएका आफन्तकाे खाेजिमा रहेका मानिसहरूले बताएकाछन्  ।

भेटिएका शव मध्ये ३ महिला ६ पुरूष गरी ९ जनाकाे परिवार द्वारा पहिचान भई शवकाे सनाखत गरी बुझाउने काम भएकाे जिप्रका नवलपरासी पूर्वले जनाएको छ।

काठमाडौँ ।

बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रबाट सङ्कलन गरिएका तर पहिचान हुन नसकेका शवलाई सरकारले जमिनमुनि व्यवस्थापन गर्न थालेको छ। ‘पहिचान नभएका तथा बेवारिसे शव व्यवस्थापन (पहिलो संशोधन) निर्देशिका, २०८३’ अनुसार पहिचान नखुलेका शवलाई वैज्ञानिक प्रक्रियाबाट व्यवस्थापन गर्न लागिएको हो।

शव व्यवस्थापन गर्नुअघि डिएनए नमुनालगायत भविष्यमा पहिचान गर्न आवश्यक पर्ने प्रमाण तथा विवरण सुरक्षित राखिने सरकारले जनाएको छ। यसरी सुरक्षित राखिएको डिएनए नमुना र अभिलेखका आधारमा भविष्यमा आफन्तले दाबी गरेमा वैज्ञानिक परीक्षणमार्फत शवको पहिचान गर्न सकिनेछ।

गृह मन्त्रालयका प्रवक्ता आनन्द काफ्लेले शव व्यवस्थापनका क्रममा निर्देशिकामा उल्लेखित सबै प्रक्रिया पालना गरिएको बताएका छन् । उनले शव जमिनमुनि व्यवस्थापन गरिएको विषयलाई लिएर भ्रम सिर्जना नगर्न आग्रह गरेका छन् ।

“हामीले शव जमिनमुनि व्यवस्थापन गर्दा निर्देशिका पालना गरेका छौँ। त्यति मात्रै होइन, वैज्ञानिक प्रक्रियासमेत पूरा गरेका छौँ,” उनले भने।

उनका अनुसार पहिचान नभएका शवको डिएनए नमुना, विवरण तथा अन्य आवश्यक प्रमाण सुरक्षित राखिने भएकाले भविष्यमा पहिचान गर्न कुनै समस्या हुँदैन।

लामो समय शव राख्दा स्वास्थ्य जोखिम

पहिचान हुन नसकेका शव लामो समयसम्म व्यवस्थापन नगरी राख्दा वातावरणीय तथा जनस्वास्थ्यमा असर पर्न सक्ने स्वास्थ्य विज्ञहरूले बताएका छन्।

स्वास्थ्य सेवा विभागअन्तर्गतको इपिडेमियोलोजी तथा रोग नियन्त्रण महाशाखाका जनस्वास्थ्यविद् डा अमृत पोखरेलले शव लामो समयसम्म अलपत्र अवस्थामा राख्दा स्वास्थ्य तथा वातावरणीय जोखिम बढ्ने भएकाले वैज्ञानिक विधिबाट व्यवस्थापन आवश्यक रहेको बताए।

उनका अनुसार पहिचान नभएका शव तथा मानव अङ्गबाट डिएनए नमुना सङ्कलन गरी सुरक्षित राख्दै जमिनमुनि व्यवस्थापन गर्नु वैज्ञानिक र जिम्मेवार कदम हो।

आफन्तले कसरी पहिचान गर्ने?

सरकारले प्रत्येक पहिचान नभएको शवको डिएनए नमुना सुरक्षित राख्ने व्यवस्था गरेको छ। साथै, प्रत्येक शवलाई छुट्टै र विशिष्ट सङ्केत नम्बर प्रदान गरिनेछ।

शवको विवरण, सङ्केत नम्बर र डिएनए नमुनासहितको अभिलेख सुरक्षित राखिने भएकाले भविष्यमा कसैले आफ्नो आफन्त भएको दाबी गरेमा वैज्ञानिक परीक्षणमार्फत पहिचान गर्न सकिनेछ।

अर्थात्, शव जमिनमुनि व्यवस्थापन गरिए पनि भविष्यमा पहिचानका लागि आवश्यक पर्ने वैज्ञानिक प्रमाण भने सुरक्षित रहनेछ।

पहिचान खुलेपछि शव निकाल्न मिल्छ

संशोधित निर्देशिकाले भविष्यमा हकवाला पहिचान भएमा जमिनमुनि व्यवस्थापन गरिएको शव वा मानव अङ्ग उत्खनन गरी सम्मानपूर्वक परिवारलाई बुझाउनुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरेको छ।

यसका साथै, विपद्का कारण मृत्यु भएको पुष्टि भएपछि पहिचानका लागि आवश्यक परीक्षण गर्ने प्रक्रियालाई पनि संशोधित निर्देशिकाले सहज बनाएको छ।

यसले एकातर्फ लामो समयसम्म शव अलपत्र राख्दा उत्पन्न हुन सक्ने स्वास्थ्य तथा वातावरणीय जोखिम न्यूनीकरण गर्ने र अर्कोतर्फ भविष्यमा आफन्त पहिचान भएमा वैज्ञानिक प्रमाणका आधारमा शव परिवारलाई हस्तान्तरण गर्ने व्यवस्था सुनिश्चित गरेको छ।

दशरथ रंशालाको एक कुनामा रहेको मिनी कभर्डहलभित्र जब मुसलधारे पानी पर्छ, तब आकाशमात्र वर्षंदैन, नेपाली उसु खेलाडीहरूका सपनाहरू पनि छताछुल्ल भएर चुहिन्छन् । चुहिने छानो, पानी जमेर जलमग्न बनेको म्याट, अनि चिसोले कठ्याङ्ग्रिने पर्खालहरू, यो कुनै सामान्य अभावको वास्तविकतामात्र होइन, एसियाली खेलकुदजस्तो महादेशीय सर्वोच्च खेल मञ्चमा देशको झण्डा फहराउने दृढ संकल्प बोकेका नेपाली उसु खेलाडीको दैनिक नियति हो । एकातिर राष्ट्रिय खेलकुद परिषद् (राखेप) ले ‘मिसन २०२६’ को भव्य खाका कोरेर जापानको आइची–नागोया एसियाडमा स्वर्ण पदक जित्ने महत्वकांक्षी लक्ष्य सार्वजनिक गर्छ, अर्कातिर, त्यही लक्ष्यका मुख्य सारथी मानिएका सान्सौँ (सान्दा) का खेलाडीहरू एउटा गुणस्तरीय म्याट र ओभानो छानोका लागि याचना गरिरहेका छन् । १९औँ दक्षिण एसियाली खेलकुदका लागि ल्याइएको पुरानो म्याटमा हिलो र पानी पन्छाउँदै बिहान र बेलुका गरी चार घण्टा पसिना बगाउने प्रशिक्षक तुलसीनन्द बज्राचार्य, प्रकाश महर्जन र उनीहरूका ११ जना प्रतिबद्ध खेलाडीहरूको आँखामा भने निराशा होइन, एउटा अदम्य जितको भोक टल्किएको देखिन्छ ।

सन् १९९० को बेइजिङ एसियाडबाट सुरु भएको नेपाली उसुको ३६ वर्षे यात्रा केवल एउटा खेल अभियानमात्र होइन, अभावको पहाड पन्छाउँदै साँचिएको अधुरो पदकको करुण र ओजस्वी सपना पनि हो । दक्षिण एसियाली खेलकुद (साग) को म्याटमा जब नेपाली फाइटरहरू ओर्लिन्छन्, तब सफलता र पदकले सुसज्जित हुने गर्दछन् । घरेलु भूमि र क्षेत्रीय स्तरमा नेपाल उसुको निर्विकल्प ‘पावरहाउस’ हो । तर, जब यही टोली चीन, कोरिया जस्ता उसुका महाशक्ति राष्ट्रहरू सम्मिलित एसियाडको विश्वस्तरीय प्रतिस्पर्धात्मक महासागरमा पाइला टेक्छ, त्यहाँको कथा अर्कै बनिदिन्छ । सागमा स्वर्ण जितेर देशको शिर उचो पार्ने नीमा घर्ती मगर, विजय सिञ्जाली, र सुस्मिता तामाङजस्ता कर्मठ खेलाडीहरूले हरेक संस्करणमा आफ्नो सर्वस्व सुम्पेका छन् । तर, एसियाडको त्यो ऐतिहासिक पदक भने अझै पनि नेपाली खेलप्रेमीका लागि केवल एउटा टाढाको सपना बनेको छ । ३६ वर्षको यो निरन्तर प्रयासमा एउटा पनि पदक हात नलाग्नु खेलाडीको क्षमता वा समर्पणको कमी होइन, खेल प्रविधिको अभाव र दीर्घकालीन नीतिको खडेरीको प्रत्यक्ष परिणाम हो ।

नेपाली उसुभित्रको आन्तरिक विभेद र पूर्वाधारको दयनीय चित्रले खेलाडीहरूको मन झनै अमिलो बनाउँछ । ‘मिसन २०२६’ अन्तर्गत थाउलो विधाका खेलाडीहरू विजय सिञ्जाली, सुस्मिता तामाङ, दीपक हमाल, हरिप्रसाद गोले, राजीव तामाङ र सविता राई नेपालस्थित चिनियाँ दूतावासको सहयोगमा चीनको युनान विश्वविद्यालयमा एक महिनाको अत्याधुनिक वैदेशिक प्रशिक्षण पूरा गरेर फर्किएका छन् । प्रकाश महर्जनको मुख्य प्रशिक्षणमा रहेका उनीहरूले अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरको एक्सपोजर पाएका छन् । २०१४ को इन्चोन एसियाडदेखि निरन्तर चौथोपटक एसियाडको तयारीमा रहेकी अनुभवी खेलाडी सुस्मिता तामाङ चीनको आधुनिक तालिमले आफ्नो खेल कौशल र ज्ञानमा निखार ल्याएको बताउँछिन् । तर, उनी पनि काठमाडौँ फर्केपछि सिनामंगलको होटलबाट गाडीमा रंगशाला धाइरहँदा चुहिने हल र भिजेको म्याट देख्दा मर्माहत हुन्छिन् । दुःखको कुरा त के छ भने, सान्सौँ (फाइट) विधाका रोहित चुनारो, अमर सुनार, सञ्जीव महर्जन, मुकेश पण्डित र रिता ठकुल्लाले भने यस्तो कुनै वैदेशिक एक्सपोजर पाउन सकेका छैनन् ।

एकै छानोमुनि थाउलोले वैदेशिक तालिम पाउँदा सान्सौँका खेलाडीले भने त्रिपुरेश्वरकै हिलाम्मे कभर्डहलमा चित्त बुझाउनु परेको छ । यद्यपि, अभावले नै प्रतिभालाई निखार्छ भन्ने जीवित उदाहरण बनेका छन् नवप्रवेशी खेलाडी मुकेश पण्डित । विगत नौ वर्षदेखि निरन्तर पसिना बगाइरहेका मुकेशले २०१८ र २०२२ को एसियाड छनोटमा भोगेको हारलाई शक्तिमा बदल्दै यसपटक दुईवटा एसियाड खेलिसकेका अनुभवी खेलाडी मंगलप्रसाद थारूलाई पराजित गरेर टोलीमा स्थान बनाएका हुन् । पहिलोपटक अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पाइला टेक्न लागेका मुकेश र रिता ठकुल्लाको भनाइमा स्वर्णको दाबीभन्दा पनि आफ्नो जीवनकै उत्कृष्ट र स्मरणीय पर्फर्मेन्स दिने अदम्य आत्मविश्वास छ । उता, अघिल्लो संस्करणको हारबाट पाठ सिकेका अमर सुनार, रोहित चुनारो र सञ्जीव महर्जन त्यो पुराना अनुभवलाई पदकमा बदल्न मरिहत्ते गरिरहेका छन् ।

नेपाली उसुको विकासमा अर्को ठूलो पर्खाल बनेर उभिएको छ प्रशासकीय राजनीति र दुईवटा महासंघको अस्तित्व । राष्ट्रिय र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मान्यताको नाममा विभाजित दुई उसु संघको विवादका कारण खेलाडीहरू पिसिन बाध्य छन् । उसुको उद्गमस्थल चीन, अनि इरान र भियतनामजस्ता देशहरू जहाँ ‘स्पोट्र्स साइन्स’, भिडियो एनालाइटिक्स, बायोमेकानिक्स र न्युट्रिसन एक्सपर्टसहित वर्षभरि नै अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय ‘टेस्ट म्याच’ गराइन्छ, ती देशका आधुनिक सुसज्जित खेलाडीहरूसँग नेपालका यी निहत्था र स्रोतविहीन योद्धाहरूले केवल आफ्नो आत्मबल र हिम्मतका भरमा भिड्नुपरेको छ ।

नेपालमा दीर्घकालीन खेलाडी विकास योजनाको अभाव छ । विभागीय टोली (नेपाल पुलिस, त्रिभुवन आर्मी, र सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल) बाहेकका प्रतिभाशाली खेलाडीहरूले केवल खेल खेलेर जीविकोपार्जन गर्न नसक्दा उमेर छँदै खेल छाड्न वा वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा पलायन हुन बाध्य छन् । साथै, ताओलु जस्तो प्राविधिक विधामा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरका ‘ए–ग्रेड’ निर्णायकको नेपाली उपस्थिति नहुँदा पनि हाम्रा खेलाडीहरू प्राविधिक अंक प्राप्त गर्नबाट वञ्चित हुने गरेका छन् । तर, यी तमाम चुनौती, आँसु र अभावका बाबजुद आशाको दियो निभेको छैन । विजय सिञ्जालीले जापानमा आयोजित तेस्रो ताओलु विश्वकपमा ऐतिहासिक कांस्य पदक जितेर विश्व मञ्चमा नेपालको धाक जमाइसकेका छन् । यो सफलताले स्पष्ट पार्छ, नेपाली खेलाडीको प्राविधिक कौशल र भित्री हिम्मत विश्वका शीर्ष खेलाडीभन्दा कम छैन ।

जापानको आइची–नागोया एसियाड २०२६ नजिकिँदै गर्दा नेपाली उसु टोली पुनः एकपटक आफ्नो रगत र पसिनाको मूल्य माग्न म्याटमा ओर्लिँदै छ । यो ३६ वर्षे यात्रा केवल पदकको खोजीमात्र होइन, राज्यको उपेक्षा, दयनीय पूर्वाधार र प्रतिकूल परिस्थितिलाई चिर्दै इतिहास रच्ने दृढ सङ्कल्पको जीवित प्रमाण हो । जबसम्म हाम्रा खेलाडीहरूको मुटुमा जितको भोक र आँखामा राष्ट्रिय झण्डा फहराउने सपना छ, तबसम्म यो संघर्ष रोकिने छैन । चुहिने छानोमुनिबाट सुरु भएको यो यात्राले एक दिन एसियाडको पोडियम चुम्नेछ र त्यो ऐतिहासिक ‘ब्रेक थ्रु’ ले सिंगो देशको गौरवलाई नयाँ उचाइ दिनेछ ।

चिसो तथ्याङ्क र भविष्यवाणीहरूले जहिले पनि मानिसको सीमा नाप्न खोज्छन्, तर जिद्दी र अथक संकल्प बोकेका योद्धाहरूले ती सबै गणितीय समीकरणहरूलाई लत्याएर आफ्नै रगत र पसिनाले नयाँ इतिहास लेख्छन् । नेपाली मिश्रित मार्सल आट्र्स (एमएमए) का गौरवशाली नक्षत्र, ‘बझाङको बाघ’ उपनामले चिनिने रविन्द्र ढाँट यतिबेला आफ्नो खेल जीवनको सबैभन्दा ठूलो र निर्णायक मोडमा उभिएका छन् । अगस्ट २८ का दिन चीनको सांघाई इन्डोर स्टेडियममा हुने ‘रोड टू यूएफसी सिजन ५’ को बहुप्रतिक्षित ब्यान्टमवेट सेमिफाइनलमा जब रविन्द्र केज (रिङ) मा पाइला टेक्नेछन्, तब त्यहाँ केवल दुई जना लडाकुमात्र भिडिरहेका हुनेछन् । तर, खेलको पछाडि करोडौं नेपालीको अदृश्य आशा, राष्ट्रिय प्रतिष्ठा र एउटा असम्भवजस्तो लाग्ने सपनाको भारी बोकिएको हुनेछ ।

कागजमा हेर्दा रविन्द्रका प्रतिद्वन्द्वी, न्युजिल्यान्डका अपराजित फाइटर कासिब मर्डोकको पक्षमा तथ्याङ्कहरूको भारी चाङ छ । ८–० को अपराजित व्यावसायिक रेकर्ड बोकेका मर्डोकलाई विश्व प्रसिद्ध ‘टापोलोजी’ कम्युनिटीले ७९ प्रतिशत समर्थन गर्दै विजेताको रूपमा उभ्याएको छ भने १० जितर १ हारको उत्कृष्ट प्रोफेसनल रेकर्ड भएका रविन्द्रलाई मात्र २१ प्रतिशत मत दिएर ‘अन्डरडग’ को रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरेको छ । तर, एमएमएजस्तो क्रुर र कलात्मक खेलमा कागजी अंक गणित वा भर्चुअल अनुमानहरूले कहिल्यै पनि केज भित्रको वास्तविक लडाइँलाई निर्धारण गर्न सक्दैनन् । यहाँ जित हारको फैसला रणनीति, समयको सही सदुपयोग, मानसिक दृढता र एउटा घातक प्रहारले गर्छ । मकाउमा फिलिपिन्सका किम्बर्ट एलिन्टो जोनलाई दोस्रो राउन्डमै टीकेओमार्फत धुलो चटाउँदै यो सेमिफाइनल यात्रा तय गरेका रविन्द्रले आफूलाई कमजोर ठान्नेहरूलाई आफ्नो तागतले पहिले नै गतिलो जवाफ दिइसकेका छन् ।

तर, यो प्रतिस्पर्धा केवल शारीरिक तागतको लडाइँमात्र रहेन, यसले मानसिक युद्धको रूपसमेत लिइसकेको छ । न्युजिल्यान्डका फाइटर मर्डोकले सांघाई उड्नुअघि सामाजिक सञ्जालमा ‘म नेपालको राजा हुँ’ र ‘पूरै नेपाललाई निराश पार्नेछु’ जस्ता अत्यन्तै विवादास्पद र दम्भी अभिव्यक्तिहरू दिएर नेपाली समर्थकहरूको भावनामाथि लगातार प्रहार गरिरहेका छन् । विरोधीले मानसिक दबाब सिर्जना गरेर मैदानमा उत्रनुअघि नै मनोबल गिराउने यो पुरानो रणनीति हो । तर, इन्डोनेसियाको बालीमा पसिनाले नुहाउँदै, कडा जाडो र थकानलाई बेवास्ता गरेर पसिना बगाएका रविन्द्र यी सस्तो प्रचारबाजीबाट किमार्थ विचलित भएका छैनन् । मर्डोकको यो घमन्ड र दम्भको भाषालाई शब्दले होइन, आगामी अगस्ट २८ मा सांघाईको केज भित्र आफ्नो शक्तिशाली पञ्च र अदम्य कडा मिहिनेतले ठोस जवाफ दिने प्रण रबिन्द्रले गरेका छन् ।

अघिल्लोपटक ‘म्याट्रिक्स फाइट नाइट’ को ब्यान्टमवेट च्याम्पियनसिप जितेर इतिहास रचेका रविन्द्रका लागि यो केवल अर्को खेलमात्र होइन, नेपालको झन्डालाई विश्वकै सर्वोच्च एमएमए संस्था ‘यूएफसी’ को व्यावसायिक मञ्चमा सधैँका लागि स्थापित गर्ने सुनौलो अवसर हो । यो सेमिफाइनल पार गर्नु भनेको यूएफसीको आधिकारिक सम्झौता नजिक पुग्नु र करोडौं नेपाली युवाहरूको आँखामा आशाको नयाँ दियो बाल्नु हो । जब अगस्ट २८ मा काउन्ट डाउन सकिएर घण्टी बज्नेछ, तब त्यो रिङ भित्र केवल दुई खेलाडीमात्र हुने छैनन्, त्यहाँ नेपालको संघर्ष, एक गरिब तर, स्वाभिमानी पहाडको आँट र विश्वमञ्चमा केही गरेर देखाउने अदम्य हुटहुटी हुनेछ । कागजी तथ्याङ्क जस्तो सुकै होस्, तर जसले आफ्नै आँसुलाई पसिना बनाएर लड्न सिकेको छ, उसलाई कसैले रोक्न सक्दैन ।

काठमाडौं ।

रसुवा बाढीबाट प्रभावित विद्युत् आयोजनामा उद्धारका लागि आएको ६ सदस्यीय चिनियाँ सुरुङ विज्ञ टोली २१६ मेगावाटको अपर त्रिशूली–१ जलविद्युत् आयोजनाको सम्पर्कमा रहेको पाइएको छ।

यसअघि प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयले उक्त टोलीलाई माथिल्लो त्रिशूली–३ ‘बी’ आयोजनाको सुरुङमा फसेका मानिसको उद्धारका लागि परिचालन गरिएको जानकारी दिएको थियो। तर, उक्त आयोजनाको सुरुङमा मानिस नफसेको र चिनियाँ टोली आयोजनास्थलमा समेत नपुगेको व्यवस्थापनले स्पष्ट पारेको छ।

अपर त्रिशूली–१ का प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत गिरिराज अधिकारीका अनुसार चिनियाँ सुरुङ विज्ञ टोली आफूहरूको सम्पर्कमा छ। आयोजनाको सुरुङमा करिब ४ सय जना फसेको अनुमान गरिएको उनले बताए।

अपर त्रिशूली–१ को सिभिल निर्माणको काम चिनियाँ कम्पनी ‘चाइना रेलवे’ले गरिरहेको छ। सोही निर्माण कम्पनीसँगको समन्वयमा चिनियाँ सुरुङ विज्ञ टोली आएको र उनीहरू आइतबारदेखि फिल्डमा खटिने तयारीमा रहेको अधिकारीले जानकारी दिए।
